alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction causing viremia
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. Patient started carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily two weeks ago and was previously suppressed (VL <50 copies/mL on 2025-09-01). Viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. The temporal relationship between carbamazepine initiation and viral load rise strongly supports the interaction as the cause. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch from carbamazepine to valproic acid as recommended by guidelines, or consult neurology for an alternative antiepileptic that does not reduce DTG levels.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load needs guideline-based management
alerts.message: Guidelines define treatment failure as two consecutive viral loads >1,000 copies/mL and require following the viral load algorithm when not suppressed. This patient's VL of 1,240 copies/mL exceeds the >1,000 threshold. The clinician's plan does not include enhanced adherence counseling, a repeat viral load, or referral to the multidisciplinary VL review committee. The carbamazepine-DTG interaction is a likely contributor, but guideline-based blips management must still be followed.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence counseling, address the carbamazepine-DTG interaction, and repeat viral load in 3 months. Refer to VL review committee if persistently >1,000.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT and hyponatremia likely carbamazepine toxicity
alerts.message: ALT is 68 U/L (Grade 1 toxicity per guideline grading). Patient takes TDF, valproate, and carbamazepine, all hepatotoxic. Carbamazepine level is supra-therapeutic at 14 mcg/mL, making it the most likely culprit. Hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also a known carbamazepine adverse effect. Evidence against TDF attribution: creatinine is normal at 84 umol/L, and ALT is only mildly elevated. The plan to reduce carbamazepine dose is appropriate but does not address monitoring for hepatic recovery.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat ALT and sodium after dose adjustment, and file an aDSM report for the suspected adverse drug reaction.

Given the above background and taking into consider the 2021 World Health Organization guidance to monitor low-level viremia, the guidelines have been designed to carter for health facilities with capacity to utilize plasma and dried blood spot (DBS) samples at suppression cut off points of 200 copies/ mL and 400 copies/mL respectively, as shown in Figure 58. A patient who has been on ART for more than 6 months and is responding to ART is considered virally suppressed at VL <200 copies/mL and <400 copies/mL for plasma and DBS samples, respectively. Facilities should constitute a multidisciplinary VL review committees to review, track, and make decisions to optimize ART regimen by switching to second-line, third- line, or a more potent regimen.
